rationale: This is essentially the archive's best signal (BuybackFundingSource) with both legs mechanically broadened — payout to prstkc+dvc (already tested as PayoutCredibilityGate) and financing to sstk+dltis — so it reads as a cosmetic union of two archived constructs rather than a new mechanism, and the smooth, persistent dividend level will likely dominate the payout scale and pull the sort toward the known payout-yield anomaly.

Extending the funding-source contrast to gross debt retirement is a genuinely different financing action with a coherent nonnegative-scale × signed-gate construction, though the gate alone (high operating cash flow minus high equity issuance) is close to a known profitability-plus-issuance composite, so much of any resulting alpha may be a rescaled version of well-documented effects.

The ratio is non-monotone and unstable whenever five-year operating cash flow is negative or close to offsetting cumulative issuance (denominator can approach zero or turn negative, flipping the sign for the most distressed firms that the signal is supposed to short), and once winsorized it is largely a monotone repackaging of the well-known external-financing/net-issuance anomaly scaled by cash-flow profitability.

The mechanism — issuance conditioned on accrual quality — is the same one already tested as DilutionQualityGate (with the sign merely reversed by using ib−oancf instead of oancf−ib), and because every factor in the product is nonnegative and the indicator zeroes out all unprofitable firms, the long leg becomes a large tied mass of zeros rather than an economically identified group.

Rollover volume via MIN(issuance, retirement) is a quantity that all net-debt-flow signals mechanically cancel and the working-capital gate is a balance-sheet liquidity dimension absent from FF5, making this a substantively new test, though it inherits the structural fragility seen in the archived MIN-based churn signal and the working-capital gate will pick up strong industry/business-model tilts.

Multiplying a signed dividend change by a signed funding-source gate makes the sign economically incoherent in one quadrant: firms cutting dividends while heavily tapping outside capital (negative × negative) land in the long leg, and internally funded cutters land in the short leg, which directly contradicts the stated credibility mechanism.
